title: What Is Blood Pressure?
text: Blood pressure is the force exerted by circulating blood against the walls of the arteries, recorded as two numbers: systolic pressure (when the heart beats) over diastolic pressure (when the heart rests between beats), measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). A commonly cited normal reading is around 120/80 mmHg for adults, though healthy ranges vary by individual; consistently elevated readings (hypertension) increase the risk of heart disease and stroke, and should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.
